doc.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Teenage favorites: big bands and Earl Hines
summary: As an organist she favored McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Henderson, Millinder and Ellington, and credits Earl Hines with making the left hand important and playing tenths.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: When you were, let’s go back to your teen years and you started listening, there was a lot of jazz on the radio is that right?
Who were the players that grabbed your ear?

Well first of all you see I played organ. By this time I was accomplished somewhat on the organ. And so I looked at everything from an orchestral point of view. And my favorite bands at that time, when I was a teenager, were the McKinney Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson, Lucky Millinder and then Duke. I imagined Duke may have come in there earlier. And Earl “Fatha” Hines, not so much for his band but he was a remarkable pianist that really caused all jazz pianists to re-think what they were doing. He you know, the style of piano playing before Duke and before Earl Hines was that you just sort of copied what you already heard, what was already being played. It was almost ensemble rhythm and if you didn’t do that you played [scats]. Now Duke you see changed all that. But Earl Hines changed the mechanics of the playing. He was the first one, to my knowledge at least, to make the left hand important harmonically as well as melodically. And he introduced tenths, you know, he had fingers that just went on and on and on and on. So it was no task for him. Up until then, and even after he introduced the solid playing of a tenth, there was a kind of a scooping motion that pianists used [scats]—

Yeah, to get it all in because they couldn’t reach it. Duke, on the other hand, I’ll quote my piano teacher at Bush Conservatory. She was a classical pianist and didn’t know anything about jazz, conceptually, but she did say that he knew more about keyboard harmony
